newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Purchasing Mgrs August index rises to 61.0.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Purchasing Mgrs August index rises to 61.0.

text.p: The Detroit Purhasing Managers' Index rose to 61.0 in August, an 8.4 point increase over 52.6 in July, according to a survey by Comerica Bank, a unit of Comerica Inc, announced Tuesday.
An index below 50 percent signals a slowing manufacturing economy, while a reading above 50 percent suggests expansion.
The prices paid index was 52.7 in August versus 45.7 in July.
The employment component of the barometer was 54.1 in August versus 51.1 in July.

The survey of business conditions in southeastern Michigan's industrial economy showed the automotive sector was the primary contributor to the gain in August -- the best since February, said David Littmann, senior economist at Comerica.

"Purchasing managers reported brisk new order and production activity, but non-auto respondents cited increased labor shortages, ranging from unskilled workers to construction and engineering workers. It also appears that price pressures have again firmed," he said.
